column11: ⚠️⚠️ THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS DANGEROUS, AND IT IS THE PART TO CARRY: IN INSTANCE (1) THE ANALYST EXPLICITLY GUARDED THE VALUE AND THE VALUE WAS FINE. WALTER attached a caveat citing its own 4.6% chart-reading error hours earlier and wrote that an error of that size "is the entire distance between at the COVID low and comfortably above it" — then read the value to 0.14%. THE CAVEAT PROTECTED THE WRONG THING WHILE LOOKING RIGOROUS. ⇒ TIGHTENING A MEASUREMENT TOLERANCE DOES NOTHING FOR REFERENT ERROR; THEY ARE INDEPENDENT FAILURE MODES AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS INSTINCTIVE TO GUARD. ★ CHEAP TESTS, ALL OF WHICH WOULD HAVE WORKED ON AT LEAST ONE INSTANCE: (a) DOES THE PUBLISHER OWN SUPERLATIVE BOUND MY CLAIM? NAR "lowest level since JANUARY 2026" is a six-month claim and refutes a record-low read for free, before any data pull — and it also catches a secondary over-claiming it (RISMedia "lowest level in 2026" is FALSE, Jan-2026 printed 70.9 below July 71.2). (b) AM I READING ONE SURFACE AND CONCLUDING ABOUT A PUBLISHER, A SERIES, OR A MARKET? (c) HOW MANY POINTS OF THIS SERIES DO I ACTUALLY HOLD? ★ SELF-DIRECTED RULE ADOPTED: TREAT "IN THE SERIES I HOLD" (and its cousins "as far as I can see", "of the data I have") AS A RED FLAG IN MY OWN WRITING RATHER THAN AS HONEST HEDGING. If a superlative needs that clause to be true, the correct move is TO GO GET THE SERIES, not to publish the clause — the clause makes the sentence defensible and leaves the reader with the wrong belief. RELATED BUT DISTINCT FROM KB-HOMER-013 (composition masks): a composition mask is a RIGHT number about a MIXED population; a referent error is a RIGHT number about the WRONG OBJECT. Both arrive as "the number is fine, so the story is fine," but the composition fix is to decompose and the referent fix is to NAME WHAT THE NUMBER IS OF. column11: ⚠️⚠️ A CORRECTION TO MY OWN MID-ANALYSIS READ, MADE BEFORE PUBLISHING IT: I had drafted that the special-assessment carve-out is an ESCAPE HATCH — that a Florida condo which levies an assessment to fund SIRS repairs falls OUT of the ineligibility test precisely because it assessed. THAT IS TRUE OF THAT ONE BULLET AND FALSE OF THE GUIDE. The Special Assessments section immediately below reads, VERBATIM: "If the special assessment is associated with a critical repair and the issue is not remediated, the project is ineligible." => THE CARVE-OUT CHANGES WHICH TEST APPLIES, NOT WHETHER THE PROJECT IS ELIGIBLE. Funding via assessment moves the project from the $10,000 unfunded-repairs bullet into the Special Assessments test, which reaches the SAME outcome when the underlying critical repair is unremediated. Caught by reading the next section instead of stopping at the sentence containing my search term — the narrowest-refutation discipline (LESSONS: a retraction is a claim and carries the same burden). ★★ THE FINDING THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS FOR FLORIDA, AND IT DISPLACES THE DOLLAR THRESHOLD: B4-2.1-03 provides AT LEAST FOUR INDEPENDENT ROUTES to ineligibility, and the $10,000 bullet is only one of them. The one that binds FIRST in Florida carries NO DOLLAR AMOUNT AT ALL, verbatim: "any project that failed to pass state, county, or other jurisdictional mandatory inspections or certifications specific to structural safety, soundness, and habitability." FL's milestone-inspection / SIRS regime IS a state-mandated structural-safety inspection => the FL transmission channel runs through the INSPECTION-FAILURE bullet, not primarily through the $10,000 test. Routes 3 and 4: the Special Assessments test above, and the Inspection Reports test — any structural/mechanical inspection completed within 3 YEARS of the lender review must show no unaddressed critical repairs, no evacuation orders, no regulatory actions. ⇒ CONSEQUENCE FOR CORAL 2.5x-40x ARITHMETIC: the threshold it rests on is REAL, so the arithmetic is not void — but a dollar-threshold model UNDERSTATES FL exposure, because the binding constraint for an assessed, inspected FL condo is a PASS/FAIL inspection outcome that no per-unit dollar figure can capture. The $10,000 line is a FLOOR on the ineligibility channel, not a description of it. ⚠️ ALSO: this page version is 08/05/2026 — two days after the 8/3 GSE condo mandate took effect, so it is the POST-MANDATE text. Do not cite pre-8/3 vintages of B4-2.1-03 as current. ⚠️ METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING: a WebSearch summary on this exact question asserted the guide uses a $15,000 EXAMPLE and implied $10,000 was not a threshold. RAW HTML GREP FOUND EXACTLY ONE DOLLAR AMOUNT ON THE PAGE: $10,000. The summary was wrong on both halves. This is the second time the read-the-raw-artifact rule (LESSONS, Tooling) has been decisive on a Fannie Selling Guide question — summarizers regularize this document.

column5: ★★ 'PINNED' IS A PER-RUNG PROPERTY, NOT A PER-BAND ONE — AND A WHOLE-BAND AUDIT PASSES OVER EVERY INSTANCE. Rung census of my own threshold table, 21 rungs tested: 9 have never discriminated in any window I hold. The test is one question per LEVEL, not per row: has this level been crossed by EVERY observation I hold? If yes it is a label, not a signal. ⇒ On 2026-08-22 I disarmed National Foreclosures because ALL THREE of its rungs were pinned or unreachable — but the same disease is present in milder form across most of the table, and the audits that found the 8/22 defect ('does this row have levels?', 'is the comparator right?') cannot see it. ★★★ AND THE CENSUS CAUGHT ITSELF OVER-CLAIMING: 'pinned across the observations I hold' is a statement about MY SAMPLE, not the metric. Split honestly = 4 CONFIDENTLY STRUCTURAL (30-Yr Yellow >5.5%; EHS Yellow <5.0M and Orange <4.5M; FHA Yellow >8% — all multi-year facts) and 5 SAMPLE-LIMITED (Fannie Yellow; Freddie Yellow AND Orange; Builder cuts Yellow on 4 months; FHA Orange). Freddie is the warning: my own Q2 10-Q shows the non-CE SEGMENT at 0.13%, so the BLEND was plausibly under 0.40% in 2023 — that rung probably DID discriminate and I cannot see it from a 13-month file. HONEST COUNT: 4 pinned, 5 UNKNOWN, not 9 dead.
